sentences.text: Hon'ble Ms. Nand Prabha Shukla,J.
Heard Sri Akash Tyagi, learned counsel for the petitioners, Sri Kuldeep Singh Tomar, learned counsel for the respondents and learned A.G.A. for the State respondents.

Both the writ petitions have been preferred with the prayer to quash the impugned First Information Report dated 01.07.2022 registered as Case Crime No. 0077 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 323, 354, 506, 420, 406 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S. Mahila Thana, District Women Security (Commissionrate Gautam Budh Nagar) and for a direction to the respondents not to arrest the petitioners in pursuance of impugned First Information Report.
Vide order dated 18.07.2022, the matter was referred to the Mediation Centre.
As per report dated 18.11.2022, mediation completed and agreement dated 18.11.2022 was also enclosed.
On 15.02.2023 the following order was passed:-

"Heard Sri Pankaj Kumar Tyagi, learned Advocate holding brief of Sri Akash Tyagi,
learned counsel for the petitioners, Sri Kuldeep Tomar, learned counsel for the informant and learned AGA for the State.
Perusal of the record does not specify that whether the agreement is being honored by the parties or not as the same is disputed as on date.
Therefore, the matter is to be heard on merits and on individual basis.
List this case after four weeks.

Interim order, if any, is extended till the next date of listing. "
Today, both the parties are agreed that the terms of settlement agreement has not been complied.
We, therefore, proceed to hear the matter on merits.

The submission is that all alleged offences are punishable with imprisonment upto seven years,
therefore the police authorities are bound to follow the procedure laid down under Section 41-A Cr.P.C.
The petitioners have been wrongly implicated and could not be arrested.

Reliance has been placed on the judgement of Apex Court in Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar, (2014) 8 SCC 273 and Social Action Forum for Manav Adhikar Vs. Union of India, Ministry of Law and Justice and others in Writ Petition (Civil) No. 73 of 2015 with Criminal Appeal No. 1265 of 2017, Writ Petition (Criminal) No. 156 of 2017 and in Satendra Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Another, (2022) 10 SCC 51 and co-ordinate Division Bench of this Court in Vimal Kumar & 3 others Vs. State of U.P. & 3 others in 2021 (2) ACR 1147.
